Someone asked me about my view that an EU army could be potentially stronger than the US or Russian militaries saying he found the idea fairly ridiculous. Here was my response:

The European Union has a much larger population than either with a larger GDP than either. Building a stronger military than Russia wouldn't even be much of an achievement. Russia's economy is about as big as Canada's. Moreover, the nucleus for such a force already exists. What they lack is a compelling security threat to build a full fledged army though there are of course rumbles to build at least a more scaled down force acting parallel to NATO. A US-Russia alliance is about the best way to push them toward a full blown army as such an alliance would leave EU member states exposed.

The EU population is currently over 500 million. Brexit will knock that below 450 million. Still way above the US though at over 326 million.

Russia is a little over 143 million.

The EU has a larger economy than China or the US.

One could liken Europe to a sleeping giant. It'd take some incredibly stupid American politicians to wake it up though.

There is still enough nationalism in several of the constituent countries that entirely surrendering their defense to a pan-European bureaucracy would be wildly unpopular. A small proto-army might be possible much sooner, with expeditionary and peacekeeping duties handled by a force operating entirely under Brussels' control and oversight.
